readings.section: The Architecture of Justice and Economics
readings.title: The Reversion of Inheritances
readings.subtitle: The structural guarantee preventing permanent generational poverty and monopolized land accumulation.
readings.text: [Leviticus 25:24] ‘And provide for a redemption for the land, in all the land of your possession. [25] ‘When your brother becomes poor, and has sold some of his possession, and his redeemer, a close relative comes to redeem it, then he shall redeem <dn>את</dn> what his brother sold. [26] ‘And when the man has no one to redeem it, but he himself becomes able to redeem it, [27] then let him count the years since its sale, and return the remainder to the man to whom he sold it, that he shall return to his possession. [28] ‘And if his hand has not found enough to give back to him, then what was sold shall remain in the hand of him who bought it until the Year of Yoḇel. And it shall be released in the Yoḇel, and he shall return to his possession.

readings.section: The Architecture of Justice and Economics
readings.title: Redemption Limits and Levite Endowments
readings.subtitle: Establishing boundaries between permanent civil commerce and the everlasting agricultural inheritance of the priesthood.
readings.text: [Leviticus 25:29] ‘And when a man sells a house in a walled city, then his right of redemption shall be at the end of the year after it is sold. His right of redemption lasts a year. [30] ‘But if it is not redeemed within a complete year, then the house in the walled city shall be established beyond reclaim to the buyer of it, throughout his generations. It is not released in the Yoḇel. [31] ‘The houses of villages, however, which have no wall around them are reckoned as the field of the country. A right of redemption belongs to it, and they are released in the Yoḇel. [32] ‘As for the cities of the Lěvites, and the houses in the cities of their possession, the Lěvites have a right of redemption forever. [33] ‘And that which is redeemed from the Lěvites, both the sale of a house and the city of his possession shall be released in the Year of Yoḇel, because the houses in the cities of the Lěvites are their possession in the midst of the children of Yisra’ěl. [34] ‘But the field of the open land of their cities is not sold, for it is their everlasting possession.

readings.section: The Architecture of Justice and Economics
readings.title: Usury, Labor, and the Crucible of Mitsrayim
readings.subtitle: Strict mandates against profiting from a brother's distress and treating covenant members as permanent assets.
readings.text: [Leviticus 25:35] ‘And when your brother becomes poor, and his hand has failed with you, then you shall strengthen him, and he shall live with you, like a stranger or a sojourner. [36] ‘Take no interest from him, or profit, but you shall fear your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and your brother shall live with you. [37] ‘Do not lend him your silver on interest, and do not lend him your food for profit. [38] <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, to give you the land of Kena‛an, to be your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [39] ‘And when your brother who dwells by you becomes poor, and sells himself to you, do not make him serve as a slave. [40] ‘But as a hired servant, as a settler he is with you, and serves you until the Year of Yoḇel. [41] ‘And then he shall leave you, he and his children with him, and shall return to his own clan, even return to the possession of his fathers. [42] <dq>‘For they are <dn>My</dn> servants, whom <dn>I</dn> brought out of the land of Mitsrayim, they are not sold as slaves.</dq> [43] ‘Do not rule over him with harshness, but you shall fear your <dn>Elohim</dn>.

readings.section: The Architecture of Justice and Economics
readings.title: Acquisition from the Surrounding Nations
readings.subtitle: The legal distinction between the children of the covenant and bonded laborers from external nations.
readings.text: [Leviticus 25:44] ‘And your male and female slaves whom you have from the nations that are around you, from them you buy male and female slaves, [45] and also from the sons of the strangers sojourning among you, from them you buy, and from their clans who are with you, which they shall bring forth in your land, and they shall be your property. [46] ‘And you shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them as a possession, they are your slaves for all time. But over your brothers, the children of Yisra’ěl, you do not rule with harshness, one over another.

readings.section: The Architecture of Justice and Economics
readings.title: Kinsman Redemption and Divine Ownership
readings.subtitle: A mathematical framework for redeeming covenant members, based on their ultimate status as YeHoVaH's exclusive servants.
readings.text: [Leviticus 25:47] ‘Now when a sojourner or a settler with you becomes rich, and your brother with him becomes poor, and sells himself to the settler or sojourner with you, or to a member of the sojourner’s clan, [48] after he has been sold, there is a right of redemption to him – one of his brothers does redeem him, [49] or his uncle or his uncle’s son does redeem him, or anyone who is a close relative to him in his clan does redeem him, or if he is able, then he shall redeem himself. [50] ‘And he shall reckon with him who bought him: The price of his release shall be according to the number of years, from the year that he was sold to him until the Year of Yoḇel; as the days of a hired servant it is with him. [51] ‘If there are yet many years, according to them he repays the price of his redemption, from the silver of his purchase. [52] ‘And if few years are left until the Year of Yoḇel, then he shall reckon with him, and according to his years he repays him the price of his redemption. [53] ‘He is with him as a yearly hired servant, and he does not rule with harshness over him before your eyes. [54] ‘And if he is not redeemed in these years, then he shall be released in the Year of Yoḇel, he and his children with him. [55] <dq>‘Because the children of Yisra’ěl are servants to <dn>Me</dn>, they are <dn>My</dn> servants whom <dn>I</dn> brought out of the land of Mitsrayim. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq>

readings.title: The Prohibition of Images and the Promise of Yield
readings.subtitle: Aligning with the singular Creator and His structural timepieces to guarantee agricultural and environmental surplus.
readings.text: [Leviticus 26:1] <dq>‘Do not make idols for yourselves, and do not set up a carved image or a pillar for yourselves, and do not place a stone image in your land, to bow down to it. For <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [2] <dq>‘Guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> Sabbaths and reverence <dn>My</dn> set-apart place. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [3] <dq>‘If you walk in <dn>My</dn> laws and guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> commands, and shall do them,</dq> [4] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall give you rain in its season, and the land shall yield its crops, and the trees of the field yield their fruit.</dq> [5] <dq>‘And your threshing shall last till the time of the grape harvest, and the grape harvest shall last till the time of sowing. And you shall eat your bread until you have enough, and shall dwell in your land safely.</dq>

readings.title: Terrestrial Authority and the Dwelling Place
readings.subtitle: The physical manifestation of absolute security, military dominance, and the unbroken communion of the Divine Presence.
readings.text: [Leviticus 26:6] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall give peace in the land, and you shall lie down and no one make you afraid. And <dn>I</dn> shall clear the land of evil beasts, and not let the sword go through your land.</dq> [7] <dq>‘And you shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall by the sword before you.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And five of you shall pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you pursue ten thousand. And your enemies shall fall by the sword before you.</dq> [9] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall turn to you and make you fruitful, and shall increase you, and shall establish <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant with <dn>את</dn> you.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And you shall eat the old supply, and clear out the old because of the new.</dq> [11] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>My</dn> Dwelling Place in your midst, and <dn>My</dn> being shall not reject you.</dq> [12] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall walk in your midst, and shall be your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and you shall be <dn>My</dn> people.</dq> [13] <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, from being their slaves. And <dn>I</dn> have broken the bars of your yoke and made you walk upright.</dq>

readings.title: The Withdrawal of the Hedge
readings.subtitle: The calculated, progressive infiltration of disease, agricultural failure, and adversarial dominance due to systemic rebellion.
readings.text: [Leviticus 26:14] <dq>‘But if you do not obey <dn>Me</dn>, and do not do <dn>את</dn> all these commands,</dq> [15] <dq>and if you reject <dn>My</dn> laws, or if your being loathes <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> right-rulings, so that you do not do <dn>את</dn> all <dn>My</dn> commands, but break <dn>My</dn> covenant,</dq> [16] <dq><dn>I</dn> also do this to you: And <dn>I</dn> shall appoint sudden alarm over you, wasting disease and inflammation, destroying the eyes, and consuming the life. And you shall sow your seed in vain, for your enemies shall eat it.</dq> [17] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>My</dn> face against you, and you shall be smitten before your enemies. And those who hate you shall rule over you, and you shall flee when no one pursues you.</dq> [18] <dq>‘And after all this, if you do not obey <dn>Me</dn>, then <dn>I</dn> shall punish you seven times more for your sins.</dq> [19] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall break <dn>את</dn> the pride of your power, and shall make your heavens like iron and your earth like bronze.</dq> [20] <dq>‘And your strength shall be spent in vain and your land not yield its crops, nor the trees of the land yield their fruit.</dq> [21] <dq>‘And if you walk contrary to <dn>Me</dn>, and refuse to obey <dn>Me</dn>, <dn>I</dn> shall bring on you seven times more plagues, according to your sins,</dq> [22] <dq>and send wild beasts among you, which shall bereave you of your children. And <dn>I</dn> shall cut off your livestock, and make you few in number, and your highways shall be deserted.</dq>

readings.title: The Collapse of Terrestrial Sovereignty
readings.subtitle: The catastrophic economic and social implosion culminating in mass deportation and the total loss of the promised inheritance.
readings.text: [Leviticus 26:23] <dq>‘And if you are not instructed by <dn>Me</dn> by these, but walk contrary to <dn>Me</dn>,</dq> [24] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> also shall walk contrary to you, and <dn>I</dn> <dn>Myself</dn> shall strike you seven times for your sins.</dq> [25] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall bring against you a sword executing the vengeance of <dn>My</dn> covenant, and you shall gather together in your cities, and <dn>I</dn> shall send pestilence among you, and you shall be given into the hand of the enemy.</dq> [26] <dq>‘When <dn>I</dn> have cut off your supply of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven, and they shall bring back to you your bread by weight, and you shall eat and not be satisfied.</dq> [27] <dq>‘And if in spite of this, you do not obey <dn>Me</dn>, but walk contrary to <dn>Me</dn>,</dq> [28] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall walk contrary to you in wrath. And <dn>I</dn> <dn>Myself</dn> shall punish you seven times for your sins.</dq> [29] <dq>‘And you shall eat the flesh of your sons, and eat the flesh of your daughters.</dq> [30] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall destroy your high places, and cut down your sun-pillars, and put your carcasses on the carcasses of your idols. And <dn>My</dn> being shall loathe you.</dq> [31] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall turn your cities into ruins and lay your set-apart places waste, and not smell your sweet fragrances.</dq> [32] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall lay <dn>את</dn> the land waste, and your enemies who dwell in it shall be astonished at it.</dq> [33] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall scatter you among the nations and draw out a sword after you. And your land shall be desert and your cities ruins,</dq>

readings.title: The Enforced Sabbatical Rest
readings.subtitle: The mathematical extraction of unpaid rests from the land while the exiled remnant descends into psychological collapse.
readings.text: [Leviticus 26:34] <dq>and the land enjoy <dn>את</dn> its Sabbaths as long as it lies waste and you are in your enemies’ land. Then the land would rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.</dq> [35] <dq>‘As long as it lies waste it rests, for the time it did not rest on your Sabbaths when you dwelt in it.</dq> [36] <dq>‘And as for those of you who are left, <dn>I</dn> shall send faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies, and the sound of a shaken leaf shall cause them to flee. And they shall flee as though retreating from a sword, and they shall fall when no one pursues.</dq> [37] <dq>‘And they shall stumble over one another, as from before a sword, when no one pursues. And you shall be unable to stand before your enemies.</dq> [38] <dq>‘And you shall perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies shall eat you up,</dq> [39] <dq>and those of you who are left rot away in their crookedness in your enemies’ lands, and also in their fathers’ crookednesses rot away with them.</dq>

readings.section: The Architecture of Justice and Economics
readings.title: Humbled Hearts and the Eternal Guarantee
readings.subtitle: The activation of the ultimate covenantal failsafe, proving YeHoVaH's disciplined love and the impossibility of total annihilation.
readings.text: [Leviticus 26:40] <dq>‘But if they confess <dn>את</dn> their crookedness and <dn>את</dn> the crookedness of their fathers, with their trespass in which they trespassed against <dn>Me</dn>, and that they also have walked contrary to <dn>Me</dn>,</dq> [41] <dq>and that <dn>I</dn> also have walked contrary to them and have brought them into the land of their enemies – if their uncircumcised heart is then humbled, and they accept <dn>את</dn> the punishment of their crookedness,</dq> [42] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall remember <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant with Ya‛aqoḇ, and also <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant with Yitsḥaq, and also remember <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant with Aḇraham, and remember the land.</dq> [43] <dq>‘For the land was abandoned by them, and enjoying its Sabbaths while lying waste without them, and they were paying for their crookedness, because they rejected <dn>My</dn> right-rulings and because their being loathed <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> laws.</dq> [44] <dq>‘And yet for all this, when they are in the land of their enemies, <dn>I</dn> shall not reject them, nor shall <dn>I</dn> loathe them so as to destroy them and break <dn>My</dn> covenant with them. For <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [45] <dq>‘Then <dn>I</dn> shall remember for their sake the covenant of the ancestors whom <dn>I</dn> brought out of the land of Mitsrayim before the eyes of the nations to be their <dn>Elohim</dn>. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ”</dq> [46] These are the laws and the right-rulings and the Torot which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made between <dn>Himself</dn> and the children of Yisra’ěl on Mount Sinai by the hand of Mosheh.
